title: AnswerFeedback
description: `POST /v1/feedback` - what a reader thought of one answer the product gave, and where that answer was. An opinion, never a measurement: nothing here reaches a canonical view, a band or a metric, and the screens that collect it state that it is filed for a later retrain rather than acted on now. The three surfaces are the three kinds of answer the product makes - a day's forecast, a replay of a past day, and the ONS passage the corpus cited - and `subject` pins which one was on screen so a reason can be read back beside the thing it was about.

id.description: The row, so a client can say which submission it is retracting or amending. Server-assigned; a client that invents one is writing somebody else's row.

recorded_at.description: When the gateway stored it, not when the reader pressed: the second is unknowable and the first is the one a later retrain can order by.

feedback_surface.description: Which kind of answer was judged. Closed, because a fourth surface is a fourth thing to retrain on and arrives with its own subject fields rather than as a free string nobody can group by.

feedback_verdict.description: Two values and no middle: a three-point scale collects a middle that means nothing to a retrain, and a star rating collects a number whose units nobody agrees on.

feedback_subject.description: What was on screen, as the keys a later retrain would group by. Every field is optional because the surfaces do not share a coordinate: a replay has a day and a lane, an evidence card has a document and a page, and a forecast has both a lane and a gate.

lane.description: The lane directory name, when the answer came from an artifact.

artifact_id.description: The artifact that produced the answer, when the screen named one. A verdict about a forecast is a verdict about the artifact that made it.

document_code.description: The ONS document the corpus cited, for the evidence surface.

answer_feedback_request.title: AnswerFeedbackRequest
answer_feedback_request.description: The body of `POST /v1/feedback`. Named in the contract rather than assembled in a component, so the camelCase the app writes is translated to the wire's casing by the generated table - the same path every other body takes, and the reason `subject`'s keys cannot drift between the two sides.

reason.description: The reader's own words, and only ever theirs. The gateway refuses a longer one rather than truncating it: a sentence cut in half says something its writer did not.

locale.description: Which dictionary the reader was reading, so the sentence can be read back in the register it was written in.
